extracted.intended_audience: federal banking regulators, policymakers, and ABA member banks / industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: An advocacy comment letter from the American Bankers Association responding to a multi-agency proposal to amend the Volcker Rule; it sets out principles the ABA believes the agencies should follow in drafting and approving regulatory reform. Focus is on clarity, administrability, reduced burden, and timely approval to enable investment activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and clarity of implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: "a simpler, clearer approach to implementing the rule makes it easier for both banks and regulators to carry out the intent of the rule."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text and tests should be written and structured so they are straightforward to interpret and apply by both supervised entities and examiners. Prefer clear bright-line rules and unambiguous definitions over complex or multi-factor tests that create enforcement uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve, clarify, and streamline regulatory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposal is "intended to continue the Agencies’ efforts to improve, clarify, and streamline the Volcker Rule’s regulatory requirements."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating revisions, prioritize removing redundant or overlapping requirements, consolidating provisions where possible, and eliminating unnecessary procedural complexity to make compliance more efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce regulatory burden and compliance costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The existing Regulation "needlessly has complicated the statutory requirements, driving up the cost of compliance and negatively impacting economic activity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reforms by their ability to lower ongoing compliance costs for banking entities without undermining statutory objectives. Consider cost-benefit implications and seek provisions that materially reduce operational or reporting burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrability / improved agency administration and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments should "address the regulatory burden and improve agency administration and supervision."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rules that are administrable by agencies — e.g., objective standards, clear supervisory expectations, and implementable monitoring metrics — to facilitate consistent supervision and reduce discretionary uneven enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision, consistency, and objectivity in tests and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulation’s problems include "vaguely defined terms, uneven treatment, and subjective tests devised to capture improper proprietary trading and covered fund investment activity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague terminology and subjective multi-factor tests. Favor precise statutory/ regulatory definitions, consistent treatment across similar activities, and objective, observable criteria to determine covered conduct. Anti-patterns include ambiguous phrases and ad hoc or discretionary tests that produce inconsistent outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / expedited approval to enable investment for public benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of COVID-19, expedited approval of the Proposal "would allow banking entities to invest in community relief and development efforts and promote capital formation through the establishment of, and/or investment in, the proposed excluded funds described herein, including public welfare and venture capital funds."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When timing is critical (e.g., economic relief contexts), consider accelerated rulemaking or implementation timelines so regulated entities can promptly undertake beneficial investment activities. Evaluate reforms for their capacity to enable community/policy objectives promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rightsizing and tailoring regulatory framework consistent with congressional purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies’ efforts are an "important recognition of the need to rightsize and tailor the Volcker Rule’s regulatory framework."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the scope and intrusiveness of restrictions are proportionate to statutory goals; tailor requirements to the nature and risk profile of entities and activities rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach. Consider exemptions or scaled requirements where appropriate.
